sentences.text: 1 2. Challenging the award passed by the Claims Tribunal, it is submitted by counsel for the appellant that in fact the injured Rahul Mehra (AW-1) had no occasion to note down the registration number of the offending vehicle.
Even in the FIR Ex.P-2 the number of the offending vehicle was not mentioned, and it was specifically mentioned that some unknown vehicle has caused accident.
The injured Rahul Mehra in paragraph 4 of his cross examination has admitted that he do not remember the registration number of the motor cycle.
The offending vehicle was seized after 4-5 months of the accident and permanent disability of 100% as assessed by Dr. P.C Anand (AW-3) is on a higher side

,
therefore, it should not have been accepted by the Claims Tribunal.
3. Considered the submission made by counsel for the appellant.

4. From the FIR Ex.P-2, which was lodged after 4 days of the accident, it is clear that it was lodged by Head Constable Mohd. Sarif, although on the front page of FIR Ex.P-2, the name of informant is mentioned as Rahul Mehra.

In the body of the FIR, it is mentioned that after receiving a requisition from the District Hospital, Narsinghpur and on the basis of the statement made by the injured Rahul Mehra, it is clear that the accident was caused by some unknown four wheeler.

By referring to FIR Ex.P-2, it is submitted by counsel for the appellant that since the statement made by the injured before enquiry officer was first in time and in the said statement, it was mentioned that the accident has been caused by some unknown vehicle, therefore it is clear that the somersault taken by Rahul Mehra (AW-1) to claim that the accident was caused by a bolera jeep is an after thought and not reliable.
5. Considered the submission made by counsel for the appellant.
6.
In the examination-in-chief, the claimant has specifically stated that accident was caused by bolero jeep bearing registration no. MP 22 BA 0361.
However the attention of this witness was not drawn towards the contents of the FIR, which is mandatory as per the provisions of section 145 of the Evidence Act.
Unless and until a witness is granted an opportunity to explain, he cannot be criticized on the basis of his previous statement.

Since the attention of Rahul Mehra (AW-1) was not drawn towards the contents of the FIR, therefore it is difficult for this Court to disbelieve Rahul Mehra (AW-1) on the basis of FIR Ex.P-2.
7.

It is next contended by counsel for the appellant that the claimant Rahul Mehra (AW-1) has admitted in paragraph 4 of his cross examination that he do not recollect the number of the vehicle therefore it is submitted that in fact the claimant was not aware of the registration number of the offending vehicle.
8.

The submissions made by the counsel for the appellant cannot be accepted for the reason that in paragraph 4 of cross examination he was being asked with regard to the details of the motorcycle which he himself was riding whereas it is a case of claimant that his motorcycle was dashed by the offending four wheeler bearing registration No. MP 22 B.A 0361.
9.

It is next contended by counsel for the appellant that since offending vehicle was seized after 4-5 months of the accident therefore it is clear that vehicle was involved falsely with an intention to National Insurance Company Ltd. vs Rahul Mehra on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34099065/

10. Considered the submission made by counsel for the appellant.
11.
It is for the enquiry officer/investigation officer to seize the vehicle and it is for owner of the vehicle to make his vehicle available to the police.
For seizure, the claimant has no role to play.

If enquiry/investigating officer was not vigilant and was negligent in conducting investigation or the owner of the vehicle had successfully avoided seizure of his vehicle, then on the said basis the evidence of the claimant cannot be doubted.
12. It is next contended by counsel for the appellant that the Claims Tribunal has wrongly held that the injured has suffered permanent disability of 100%.
By referring to the evidence of Dr. P.C Anand (AW-3), it is submitted that Dr Anand was not the treating doctor and his assessment of permanent disability to the extent of 100% cannot be relied upon.

13. Considered the submission made by counsel for the appellant.
14.

The Supreme Court in the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and another reported in (2011)1 SCC 343 has held that in order to prove the permanent disability the claimant is required to examine either treating doctor or doctor who had issued certificate of permanent disability.

entities.text: Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and another reported in (2011)1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Dr. P.C Anand (AW- 3) had issued the certificate of permanent disability Ex.P-19.
In examination in chief he has specifically stated that he was a member of the medical board.
During the course of medical examination fracture of L-3 lumber vertibra was found and paralysis on both the legs of claimant was found.
The claimant was not in a position to stand or to walk and his permanent disability was 100%.
15. If a claimant has suffered a paralysis of his both legs and is confined to wheelchair, then permanent disability of 100% as assessed by the Claims Tribunal cannot be said to be erroneous.
16. No other argument is advanced by the counsel for the appellant.
17. Under these circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that no case is made out for interference.

Accordingly, the award dated 18.02.2017 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Narsinghpur in Claim Case No.5/2015 is hereby affirmed.
The appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.

(G.S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE tarun National Insurance Company Ltd. vs Rahul Mehra on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34099065/
